newsitem.title: USA: Wife finds perfect mate has flaw - he's a she.
newsitem.headline: Wife finds perfect mate has flaw - he's a she.

text.p: A woman who got married after a romance spawned by the Internet found four months into the union that her mate had a serious flaw -- he was a she.

Margaret Anne Hunter, of the Washington suburb of Alexandria, Virginia, met the person she thought was Thorne Wesley Jameson Groves through an on-line service, according to a report in Thursday's Washington Post.

The romance proceeded with telephone calls, visits, and then a wedding, the Post said. Groves had told Hunter that "he" had AIDS and wanted to be happily married while he was dying -- but avoided physical intimacy in order to protect Hunter.
Groves turned out to be a 26-year-old Texan woman, the lawsuit filed in a Virginia circuit court claims.
Hunter got suspicious when her husband never seemed ill, never saw doctors and never removed the hefty chest bandages that were ostensibly holding broken ribs.
The "husband," identified by the Post as Holly Anne Groves, could not be reached in her Texas hometown of Bryan.

Hunter's lawyer, Seth Guggenheim, was not available for comment on Thursday but told the Post, "Holly had such credible and detailed explanations, excuses and personal history, that as the plot of this drama was unfolding, there was nothing that gave my client or other people pause."
The suit asks for $575,000 in damages for fraud and misrepresentation. That includes the costs of the wedding, the long-distance romance, food, shelter and cable TV.
There was no word on who might get the computer in any settlement.
